arxiv-1401-1051.title: Action Minimizing Solutions of The One-Dimensional N N -Body Problem With Equal Masses Thanks: Supported partially by NSF of China
arxiv-1401-1051.creator: Xiang Yu and Shiqing Zhang
arxiv-1401-1051.description: Abstract Abstract. When we use variational methods to study the Newtonian N -body problem, the main problem is how to avoid collisions. C.Marchal got a remarkable result, that is, a path minimizing the Lagrangian action functional between two given configurations is always a true (collision-free) solution, so long as the dimension d of physical space \mathbb{R}^{d} satisfies d\geq 2 .

arxiv-1907-01685.title: Voting Rules That Are Unbiased But Not Transitive-Symmetric
arxiv-1907-01685.creator: Aadyot Bhatnagar
arxiv-1907-01685.description: Abstract We explore the relation between two natural symmetry properties of voting rules. The first is transitive-symmetry — the property of invariance to a transitive permutation group — while the second is the “unbiased” property of every voter having the same influence for all i.i.d. probability measures.

arxiv-2105-13919.title: Reward Biased Maximum Likelihood Estimation for Learning in Constrained MDPs
arxiv-2105-13919.creator: Rahul Singh
arxiv-2105-13919.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Rahul Singh. We use the Reward Biased Maximum Likelihood Estimation (RBMLE) algorithm Mete et al. 2020 to learn optimal policies for constrained Markov Decision Processes (CMDPs). arxiv-2205-11903.title: Resolution Limits of Resonant Sensors with Duffing Non-Linearity
arxiv-2205-11903.creator: Tomás Manzaneque, Murali K. Ghatkesar, Farbod Alijani, Minxing Xu, Richard A. Norte, Peter G. Steeneken
arxiv-2205-11903.description: Abstract The resolution of resonant sensors is fundamentally limited by the presence of noise. Thermomechanical noise, intrinsic to the resonator, sets the ultimate sensor performance when all other noise sources have been eliminated. For linear resonators, the sensing resolution can always be further improved by increasing the driving power.

arxiv-2206-08775.title: Dead ends on wreath products and lamplighter groups
arxiv-2206-08775.creator: Eduardo Silva
arxiv-2206-08775.description: Abstract . For any finite group A A and any finitely generated group B B , we prove that the corresponding lamplighter group A ≀ B A\wr B admits a standard generating set with unbounded depth, and that if B B is abelian then the above is true for every standard generating set.

arxiv-2504-00114.title: Multiphoton Quantum Interference at Ultracompact Inverse-Designed Multiport Beam Splitter
arxiv-2504-00114.creator: Shiang-Yu Huang, Shreya Kumar, Jeldrik Huster, Yannick Augenstein, Carsten Rockstuhl, Stefanie Barz
arxiv-2504-00114.description: Abstract Photonic quantum technologies enter a new phase when realized in photonic integrated circuits, leading to a great advance in practical applications. In the pursuit of high integration density and low circuit complexity, ultracompact devices delivered by topology optimization offer a promising solution to miniaturize these photonic systems even further.

arxiv-2504-09878.title: MCBlock: Boosting Neural Radiance Field Training Speed by MCTS-based Dynamic-Resolution Ray Sampling DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: Make sure to enter the correct conference title from your rights confirmation email; June 03–05, 2018; Woodstock, NY ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/2018/06 7151 CCS: Computi
arxiv-2504-09878.creator: Yunpeng Tan, Junlin Hao, Jiangkai Wu, Liming Liu, Qingyang Li, Xinggong Zhang
arxiv-2504-09878.description: Abstract . Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) is widely known for high-fidelity novel view synthesis. However, even the state-of-the-art NeRF model, Gaussian Splatting, requires minutes for training, far from the real-time performance required by multimedia scenarios like telemedicine. One of the obstacles is its inefficient sampling, which is only partially addressed by existing works.

arxiv-2509-11197.title: DreamNav: A Trajectory-Based Imaginative Framework for Zero-Shot Vision-and-Language Navigation
arxiv-2509-11197.creator: Yunheng Wang, Yuetong Fang, Taowen Wang, Yixiao Feng, Yawen Tan, Shuning Zhang, Peiran Liu, Yiding Ji, Renjing Xu
arxiv-2509-11197.description: Abstract Vision-and-Language Navigation in Continuous Environments (VLN-CE), which links language instructions to perception and control in the real world, is a core capability of embodied robots. Recently, large-scale pretrained foundation models have been leveraged as shared priors for perception, reasoning, and action, enabling zero-shot VLN without task-specific training.

arxiv-2602-05484.title: Clouding the Mirror: Stealthy Prompt Injection Attacks Targeting LLM-based Phishing Detection
arxiv-2602-05484.creator: Takashi Koide 1 , Hiroki Nakano 1 , Daiki Chiba 1
arxiv-2602-05484.description: Abstract Phishing sites continue to grow in volume and sophistication. Recent work leverages large language models (LLMs) to analyze URLs, HTML, and rendered content to decide whether a website is a phishing site. While these approaches are promising, LLMs are inherently vulnerable to prompt injection (PI).

pmc-10654916.title: Microfluidic investigation of pore-size dependency of barite nucleation
pmc-10654916.creator: Jenna Poonoosamy, Abdulmonem Obaied, Guido Deissmann, Nikolaos I. Prasianakis, Moritz Kindelmann, Bastian Wollenhaupt, Dirk Bosbach, Enzo Curti
pmc-10654916.description: The understanding and prediction of mineral precipitation processes in porous media are relevant for various energy-related subsurface applications. While it is well known that thermodynamic effects can inhibit crystallization in pores with sizes <0.1 µm, the retarded observation of mineral precipitation as function of pore size is less explored.

pmc-10671452.title: Linear Polyethyleneimine-Based and Metal Organic Frameworks (DUT-67) Composite Hydrogels as Efficient Sorbents for the Removal of Methyl Orange, Copper Ions, and Penicillin V
pmc-10671452.creator: Luis M Araque, Roberto Fernández de Luis, Arkaitz Fidalgo-Marijuan, Antonia Infantes-Molina, Enrique Rodríguez-Castellón, Claudio J Pérez, Guillermo J Copello, Juan M Lázaro-Martínez, Shiyang Li
pmc-10671452.description: This research explores the integration of DUT-67 metal organic frameworks into polyethyleneimine-based hydrogels to assemble a composite system with enough mechanical strength, pore structure and chemical affinity to work as a sorbent for water remediation. By varying the solvent-to-modulator ratio in a water-based synthesis path, the particle size of DUT-67 was successfully modulated from 1 μm to 200 nm.

pmc-11399153.title: The effect of hydrogen gas on the oxidative stress response in adipose tissue
pmc-11399153.creator: Batkhishig Tumurbaatar, Shinji Ogawa, Nobuhisa Nakamura, Toshiyuki Yamada, Tomomi Minato, Yoshiharu Mori, Tomokazu Saiki, Tatsuaki Matsubara, Keiko Naruse, Hisao Suda
pmc-11399153.description: Oxidative stress in adipose tissue may alter the secretion pattern of adipocytokines and potentially promote atherosclerosis. However, the therapeutic role of hydrogen in adipose tissue under oxidative stress remains unclear. In this study, subcutaneous adipose tissue (SCAT) was collected from the mid-thoracic wounds of 12 patients who underwent open-heart surgery with a mid-thoracic incision.

pmc-11434070.title: Unravelling the Roles of Bacterial Nanomachines Bistability in Pathogens’ Life Cycle
pmc-11434070.creator: Romain Gory, Nicolas Personnic, Didier Blaha, Karen Angeliki Krogfelt, Luis Cláudio Nascimento Da Silva, Afonso Gomes-Abreu
pmc-11434070.description: Bacterial nanomachines represent remarkable feats of evolutionary engineering, showcasing intricate molecular mechanisms that enable bacteria to perform a diverse array of functions essential to persist, thrive, and evolve within ecological and pathological niches. Injectosomes and bacterial flagella represent two categories of bacterial nanomachines that have been particularly well studied both at the molecular and functional levels.

pmc-11437578.title: Spatial variation and determinants of traditional birth attendants utilization among women of reproductive age in Ethiopia: Spatial and multilevel analysis study
pmc-11437578.creator: Mohammed Seid Ali, Enyew Getaneh Mekonen, Belayneh Shetie Workneh
pmc-11437578.description: Background:Traditional birth attendant utilization has become a common malpractice and a leading cause of maternal morbidity and mortality in the developing world, such as Ethiopia. Therefore, this study was aimed at determining the geospatial variation and determinant factors of traditional birth attendant utilization among mothers of reproductive age in Ethiopia.

pmc-11541280.title: Integrating Genomic Data with the Development of CRISPR-Based Point-of-Care-Testing for Bacterial Infections
pmc-11541280.creator: Thanyapat Wanitchanon, Claire Chewapreecha, Chayasith Uttamapinant
pmc-11541280.description: Purpose of ReviewBacterial infections and antibiotic resistance contribute to global mortality. Despite many infections being preventable and treatable, the lack of reliable and accessible diagnostic tools exacerbates these issues. CRISPR (Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats)-based diagnostics has emerged as a promising solution.

pmc-11593023.title: Effects of PTPN6 Gene Knockdown in SKM-1 Cells on Apoptosis, Erythroid Differentiation and Inflammations
pmc-11593023.creator: Li Yu, Xiaoli Gu, Pengjie Chen, Rui Yang, Yonggang Xu, Xiupeng Yang
pmc-11593023.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Objective: Protein tyrosine phosphatase non-receptor type 6 (PTPN6) is a cytoplasmic phosphatase that acts as a key regulatory protein in cell signaling to control inflammation and cell death. In order to investigate the role of PTPN6 in hematologic tumor myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS), this study infected SKM-1 cell line (MDS cell line) with packaged H_PTPN6-shRNA lentivirus to obtain H_PTPN6-shRNA SKM-1 stable strain. The effect of PTPN6 knockdown on apoptosis, erythroid differentiation, and inflammations in SKM-1 cell line was examined.

pmc-12397471.title: Deep learning in chromatin organization: from super-resolution microscopy to clinical applications
pmc-12397471.creator: Mikhail Rotkevich, Carlotta Viana, Maria Victoria Neguembor, Maria Pia Cosma
pmc-12397471.description: The 3D organization of the genome plays a critical role in regulating gene expression, maintaining cellular identity, and mediating responses to environmental cues. Advances in super-resolution microscopy and genomic technologies have enabled unprecedented insights into chromatin architecture at nanoscale resolution. However, the complexity and volume of data generated by these techniques necessitate innovative computational strategies for effective analysis and interpretation.

pmc-12457081.title: Changes in Pain Catastrophizing and Related Outcomes Following a Single-Session Empowered Relief Intervention Delivered by Physical Therapists in Workers with Low Back Pain: A Pilot Study
pmc-12457081.creator: Junie S Carrière, Marie-France Coutu, Beth D Darnall, Guillaume Léonard, Marie-Pier Royer, Mei Yue Li, Martine Bordeleau, Marie-José Durand
pmc-12457081.description: PurposeLow back pain is among the most prevalent pain conditions. Cognitive behavioral therapy reduces the negative effects of low back pain, but access to treatment is limited. Empowered Relief is a 2-hour single-session pain management skills intervention that has demonstrated efficacy at improving pain outcomes in individuals with chronic low back pain.

pmc-13127372.title: Functional characterization and mechanistic basis of antifungal and plant growth-promoting traits of Streptomyces sp. LZZY-S40
pmc-13127372.creator: Lan Ye, Pinjiao Jin, Zhenhua Liu, Dongmiao Qin, Haolin Wang, Liyang Chu
pmc-13127372.description: Biological control agents (BCAs) represent a sustainable and environmentally benign alternative to synthetic chemical pesticides in modern agriculture. Among these, Streptomyces species are widely recognized for their ability to suppress phytopathogens and promote plant growth through diverse functional traits. In this study, a Streptomyces strain designated LZZY-S40 (=CGMCC No.

pmc-13239491.title: MUSeg‐PSV: A Real‐Time Deep‐Learning Segmentation of the Prostate Gland and Seminal Vesicles on 29‐MHz Micro‐Ultrasound
pmc-13239491.creator: Ludovica Cella, Marco Paciotti, Giacomo Cavadini, Luca Di Stefano, Pier Paolo Avolio, Vittorio Fasulo, Andrea Piccolini, Cesare Saitta, Edoardo Beatrici, Rafal Kocielnik, Andrew J. Hung, Alberto Saita, Paolo Casale, Massimo Lazzeri, Giovanni Lughezzani, Nicolò Maria Buffi
pmc-13239491.description: ObjectivesThis study aimed to develop and evaluate MUSeg‐PSV, a real‐time deep‐learning framework for segmentation of the prostate gland and seminal vesicles on 29‐MHz micro‐ultrasound (MicroUS), intended to support anatomical orientation during MicroUS‐guided prostate biopsy and local staging of prostate cancer.

pmc-13297129.title: Printed Organic Memristive Device on Rigid and Flexible Supports for Neuromorphic Applications
pmc-13297129.creator: Davide Vurro, Salvatore Del Basso, Simone Luigi Marasso, Alberto Ballesio, Giuseppe Tarabella, Pasquale D’Angelo, Victor Erokhin

pmc-13521183.title: Interpretable Deep Learning of Molecule‐Solvent Interactions Using a Solvatochromic Subgroup Contribution Framework
pmc-13521183.creator: Jinyong Park, Minhi Han, Kiwoong Lee, Seokwoo Kim, Sungnam Park
pmc-13521183.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Solvent effects critically influence the photophysical and optical properties of molecules in solution, yet a quantitative and interpretable description of solvent effects remains a long‐standing challenge. In this study, to quantitatively understand and chemically interpret solvatochromism, deep learning (DL) models based on the solvatochromic subgroup contribution (SSC) framework were introduced, which describes solvatochromic shifts through localized interactions between molecular subgroups and the surrounding solvent.

pmc-13536833.title: The gut neuroepithelial unit as a neurodegeneration-relevant interface in the gut–brain axis
pmc-13536833.creator: Siqi Guo, Rui Guo, Qingyu Zhang, Liyuan Fu, Huaxu Zhu, Qichun Zhang
pmc-13536833.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Neurodegenerative diseases are increasingly linked to abnormalities in the gut–brain axis, yet the local intestinal interface at which luminal and mucosal perturbations are related with the central nervous system remains poorly defined. The gut neuroepithelial unit (GNU) is proposed as a localized mucosal signalling interface composed of sensory epithelial cells, enteric neurons, glia and adjacent immune-stromal elements that detect, encode and route intestinal information into neural, endocrine and immune outputs.
